candidates.requirement: Exercise supported incremental number parsing across calls to json_tokener_parse_ex on the same tokener.
candidates.target_route: LLVMFuzzerTestOneInput creates a tokener, passes the entire fuzzer buffer to one json_tokener_parse_ex call, then frees the tokener.
candidates.failure_condition: No input can make the target resume a saved exponent on a second call, so the g0003 state reconstruction is unreachable.
candidates.alternative_paths: A single input can parse the same completed number, but cannot exercise restoration from previously saved tokener state; there is no second call or helper route.

candidates.requirement: Make the parser's supported strict-mode treatment of incomplete exponents reachable under the target's parse_ex operation.
candidates.target_route: The target uses json_tokener_new and calls json_tokener_parse_ex without setting flags; the constructor zero-initializes tokener state.
candidates.failure_condition: Inputs such as "[0e]" always follow the default-mode trimming route; strict-mode rejection cannot be selected by any fuzzer bytes.
candidates.alternative_paths: Default-mode parsing is not equivalent to strict-mode rejection, and the complete target has no flag setter or alternate tokener construction route.

before.requirement: Complete a valid exponent-bearing number across parse_ex calls on one tokener.
before.reason: Before the change, an unfinished number is saved for a later call. For the same split "[0e" then "-1]", the old number state permits the sign at the start of the second call; the harness has no second call.

after.requirement: Complete a valid exponent-bearing number across parse_ex calls on one tokener.
after.reason: The added state restoration supports the same incremental operation, but the unchanged harness still makes only one parse call before freeing the tokener.

claims.reason: The tuple is incremental completion of a valid exponent. Both parser versions support it, and the same single-call harness constraint blocks it on both sides.

before.requirement: Reach strict-mode rejection of an incomplete exponent such as "[0e]".
before.reason: The old number path has no incomplete-exponent check before its prefix-accepting json_parse_double call. This specific strict-mode rejection was not a supported behavior of the before version.

after.requirement: Reach strict-mode rejection of an incomplete exponent such as "[0e]".
after.reason: Strict mode bypasses the new trimming step, and length-aware conversion rejects the incomplete exponent. The unchanged harness leaves the tokener at default flags.

claims.reason: The same strict-mode rejection tuple is not required before and is required after. The harness's absent flag setup becomes a blocker only after that behavior exists.
